requirements.title: Severity classification
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall define a Severity type with INFO, WARNING, and ERROR levels that serialises as a string and is value-compatible with every x-FuSa tool's severity scheme.

requirements.title: Severity ranking
requirements.text: Severity.Rank shall return a strictly increasing ordinal for INFO < WARNING < ERROR and zero for any unknown value, to support comparison and sorting.

requirements.title: Language identification
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall define a Language type identifying each supported language (go, c, cpp, rust, python).

requirements.title: Attributable finding
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall represent each normalised finding with the originating Language and Tool so findings remain attributable after being merged across languages.

requirements.title: Finding location
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall record the file, and optional line and column, identifying the origin of each finding.

requirements.title: Comparable sentinel errors
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall expose its failure conditions as sentinel errors suitable for comparison with errors.Is.

requirements.title: Missing configuration error
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall return ErrNoConfig when no .fusaops.json configuration file is present.

requirements.title: Invalid configuration error
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall return ErrInvalidConfig when the configuration is malformed.

requirements.title: No applicable adapters error
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall return ErrNoAdapters when no detected language can be handled by any registered adapter.

requirements.title: Check failure error
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall expose ErrCheckFailed to signal that one or more ERROR-severity findings exist in the aggregated report.

requirements.title: Project configuration model
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall define a configuration model capturing project identity, adapter selection, and report preferences.

requirements.title: Adapter restriction
requirements.text: The configuration shall allow restricting which adapters run via an explicit adapter list, where an empty list means all applicable adapters.

requirements.title: Default configuration
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall provide a valid starter configuration for a named project.

requirements.title: Configuration load
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall load and validate configuration from a JSON file, returning ErrNoConfig when the file is absent.

requirements.title: Configuration save
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall serialise configuration to indented JSON on disk.

requirements.title: Configuration validation
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall reject configuration missing a version or project name, or specifying an unsupported report format.

requirements.title: Adapter interface
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall define an Adapter interface abstracting a single language-specific x-FuSa tool by name, language, tool, detection, availability, and check.

requirements.title: Generic command adapter
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall provide a generic adapter implementation shared by every x-FuSa tool that differs only in configured metadata.

requirements.title: Tool availability
requirements.text: An adapter shall report whether its tool binary resolves on PATH.

requirements.title: Language detection
requirements.text: An adapter shall detect whether its language is present under a root by source extension, skipping VCS, build, and vendor directories.

requirements.title: Tool execution
requirements.text: An adapter shall run its tool's machine-readable check and return normalised findings, treating a non-zero tool exit that signals findings as success.

requirements.title: Report normalisation
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall decode a tool's JSON report into findings tagged with the originating language and tool, normalising unknown severities to INFO rather than dropping them.

requirements.title: Adapter registry
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall maintain a registry of adapters keyed by tool name, rejecting nil or duplicate registrations.

requirements.title: Applicable adapters
requirements.text: The registry shall return the adapters whose language is detected under a given root.

requirements.title: Default registry
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall expose a package-level default registry populated by the built-in adapters.

requirements.title: go-FuSa adapter
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall register an adapter for go-FuSa handling Go (.go) projects via the gofusa tool.

requirements.title: c-FuSa adapter
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall register an adapter for c-FuSa handling C (.c) projects via the cfusa tool, excluding ambiguous headers from detection.

requirements.title: cpp-FuSa adapter
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall register an adapter for cpp-FuSa handling C++ projects via the cpfusa tool.

requirements.title: Language extension map
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall map each supported language to its source file extensions.

requirements.title: Detected languages
requirements.text: A scan result shall report the detected languages in deterministic order.

requirements.title: Repository scan
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall count source files per language under a root, skipping VCS, build, vendor, and excluded directories, and omitting languages with no files.

requirements.title: Orchestration options
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall accept orchestration options for project name, adapter restriction, and whether at least one installed tool is required.

requirements.title: Orchestration runner
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall provide an orchestration runner backed by an adapter registry, defaulting to the package-level registry.

requirements.title: Multi-language run
requirements.text: The orchestrator shall run every applicable installed adapter, record applicable-but-uninstalled tools as skipped components, aggregate the results, and return ErrNoAdapters when none apply.

requirements.title: Finding summary
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall summarise findings as total, error, warning, and info counts.

requirements.title: Aggregate status
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall derive a PASS/WARN/FAIL verdict from a summary: FAIL on any error, WARN on any warning, otherwise PASS.

requirements.title: Report component
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall represent each language's contribution as a component recording its tool, availability, skip reason, findings, and summary.

requirements.title: Aggregate report
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall define a top-level multi-language report containing all components and an overall summary.

requirements.title: Report assembly
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall assemble an aggregate report from components, computing per-component and overall summaries, with components ordered deterministically.

requirements.title: Error detection
requirements.text: The aggregate report shall report whether any component produced an ERROR-severity finding.

requirements.title: Format dispatch
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall render the aggregate report in text, JSON, HTML, or SARIF format, rejecting unsupported formats.

requirements.title: Report to file
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall write the aggregate report to a file, or to standard output when no path is given.

requirements.title: JSON rendering
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall render the aggregate report as indented JSON.

requirements.title: Text rendering
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall render a human-readable plain-text aggregate report.

requirements.title: SARIF rendering
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall render the aggregate report as SARIF 2.1.0 with one run per component for GitHub Code Scanning.

requirements.title: HTML dashboard rendering
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall render a self-contained HTML dashboard with no external dependencies.

requirements.title: Dashboard server
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall provide a web server exposing the aggregated multi-language report.

requirements.title: Server construction
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall construct a server bound to a root, orchestration runner, and options.

requirements.title: Report computation
requirements.text: The server shall compute and cache the aggregate report for fast serving and on-demand refresh.

requirements.title: HTTP routes
requirements.text: The server shall expose dashboard (/), JSON API (/api/report), refresh (/refresh), and health (/healthz) routes.

requirements.title: Serve
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall compute the initial report then serve the dashboard on a configured listener or address.

requirements.title: Command dispatch
requirements.text: The fusaops CLI shall dispatch a single invocation to the requested subcommand and return a process exit code.

requirements.title: Usage help
requirements.text: The fusaops CLI shall print top-level usage on request and on invalid invocation.

requirements.title: Version command
requirements.text: fusaops version shall print the FuSaOps version.

requirements.title: Init command
requirements.text: fusaops init shall write a starter .fusaops.json, refusing to overwrite an existing file without --force.

requirements.title: Scan command
requirements.text: fusaops scan shall report detected languages and applicable adapters with installation status.

requirements.title: Adapters command
requirements.text: fusaops adapters shall list every registered adapter and whether its tool is installed.

requirements.title: Option resolution
requirements.text: The CLI shall resolve the absolute root and merge any .fusaops.json, treating a missing configuration as non-fatal.

requirements.title: Check command
requirements.text: fusaops check shall run every applicable tool, render the aggregate report, and exit non-zero on ERROR findings, or on WARNING findings under --strict.

requirements.title: Report command
requirements.text: fusaops report shall generate an aggregate report to a file or standard output without failing on findings.

requirements.title: Serve command
requirements.text: fusaops serve shall launch the web dashboard on a configured address.

requirements.title: Trace command
requirements.text: fusaops trace shall roll up cross-language requirement traceability and qualification, render it (text/json/html), and exit non-zero under --strict when any requirement is untraced or untested.

requirements.title: SBOM command
requirements.text: fusaops sbom shall merge every applicable tool's SBOM into one cross-language bill of materials rendered as json, text, or SPDX 2.3.

requirements.title: Audit-pack command
requirements.text: fusaops audit-pack shall bundle every applicable tool's audit-pack together with the FuSaOps cross-language evidence into a single ZIP.

requirements.title: Requirement decode
requirements.text: The trace package shall decode a requirement entry (id, title, standard, level, ASIL) from a tool's traceability matrix.

requirements.title: Annotation tag decode
requirements.text: The trace package shall decode requirement and test annotation tags, distinguishing their kind.

requirements.title: Coverage figures
requirements.text: The trace package shall decode the total, traced, and tested requirement counts from a tool's matrix.

requirements.title: Matrix model
requirements.text: The trace package shall model a tool's traceability matrix as requirements, tags, and coverage.

requirements.title: Qualification summary
requirements.text: The trace package shall model a tool's qualification summary with total, passed, and failed case counts.

requirements.title: Component trace
requirements.text: The trace package shall represent each language's contribution with its tool, availability, skip reason, coverage, requirements, and qualification.

requirements.title: Coverage percentages
requirements.text: The trace package shall compute traced and tested percentages per component, treating zero requirements as fully covered.

requirements.title: Aggregate coverage
requirements.text: The trace package shall sum coverage across components into aggregate totals and percentages.

requirements.title: Aggregate matrix model
requirements.text: The trace package shall model the cross-language roll-up with generation time, root, project, components, and aggregate coverage.

requirements.title: Aggregate construction
requirements.text: The trace package shall build the aggregate deterministically (components sorted by tool), excluding skipped components from coverage totals so gaps stay visible.

requirements.title: Gap status
requirements.text: The trace package shall report a PASS/GAP status that fails when any requirement across all languages is untraced or untested.

requirements.title: Matrix rendering
requirements.text: The trace package shall render the aggregate to a writer or file in text, json, or html, rejecting unknown formats.

requirements.title: Matrix JSON
requirements.text: The trace package shall render the aggregate as indented JSON.

requirements.title: Matrix text
requirements.text: The trace package shall render a human-readable text view with per-component and total coverage and status.

requirements.title: Matrix HTML
requirements.text: The trace package shall render a self-contained, dependency-free HTML traceability dashboard.

requirements.title: Normalised package
requirements.text: The sbom package shall represent a dependency as name, version, optional hash, and originating language.

requirements.title: Tool SBOM decode
requirements.text: The sbom package shall decode a tool's SBOM document (module, go version, component packages).

requirements.title: Component SBOM
requirements.text: The sbom package shall represent each language's SBOM contribution with tool, availability, skip reason, module, and packages.

requirements.title: Aggregate SBOM model
requirements.text: The sbom package shall model the merged cross-language SBOM with generation time, root, project, components, packages, and total count.

requirements.title: SBOM merge
requirements.text: The sbom package shall merge component packages, de-duplicating on name and version, deterministically sorted, preserving the first contributing language.

requirements.title: SBOM rendering
requirements.text: The sbom package shall render the aggregate to a writer or file in json, text, or spdx, rejecting unknown formats.

requirements.title: SBOM JSON
requirements.text: The sbom package shall render the aggregate as indented native JSON.

requirements.title: SBOM text
requirements.text: The sbom package shall render a human-readable text view of components and merged packages.

requirements.title: SPDX rendering
requirements.text: The sbom package shall render a valid SPDX 2.3 JSON document with a DESCRIBES relationship per package and syntactically valid SPDX identifiers.

requirements.title: Pack source
requirements.text: The auditpack package shall accept bundle sources supplied either by file path or in-memory data, keyed by archive path.

requirements.title: Pack entry integrity
requirements.text: The auditpack package shall record each packed file's path, size, and SHA-256 hash.

requirements.title: Pack manifest
requirements.text: The auditpack package shall write a manifest.json index naming the tool, version, project, and packed files.

requirements.title: Deterministic packing
requirements.text: The auditpack package shall write a deterministic ZIP with sources sorted by archive path, failing hard if any source content cannot be read so no evidence is silently omitted.

requirements.title: JSON source helper
requirements.text: The auditpack package shall provide a helper that marshals a value into an in-memory JSON bundle source.

requirements.title: Adapter capabilities
requirements.text: FuSaOps shall define optional capability interfaces (Tracer, Qualifier, SBOMer, Packer) so an adapter can contribute trace, qualification, SBOM, and audit-pack evidence when its tool supports them.

requirements.title: Adapter trace
requirements.text: A command adapter shall produce a traceability matrix by running its tool's trace command and decoding the JSON output.

requirements.title: Adapter qualify
requirements.text: A command adapter shall produce a qualification summary by running its tool's qualify command and decoding the report file.

requirements.title: Adapter SBOM
requirements.text: A command adapter shall produce an SBOM by running its tool's release command and decoding the generated sbom.json.

requirements.title: Adapter audit-pack
requirements.text: A command adapter shall produce a per-tool audit-pack ZIP by running its tool's audit-pack command and confirming the file was written.

requirements.title: Trace roll-up
requirements.text: The orchestrator shall roll every applicable tool's trace and qualification into one cross-language aggregate, recording skipped components.

requirements.title: SBOM roll-up
requirements.text: The orchestrator shall merge every applicable tool's SBOM into one cross-language aggregate, recording skipped components.

requirements.title: Audit-pack roll-up
requirements.text: The orchestrator shall bundle every applicable tool's audit-pack with the FuSaOps cross-language evidence into one ZIP, always including the FuSaOps-level artefacts.

requirements.title: Conformance level types
requirements.text: The conform package shall define Level (MUST/SHOULD/MAY) and Status (PASS/FAIL/SKIP) types matching RFC 2119.

requirements.title: Conformance result
requirements.text: The conform package shall represent each check outcome with id, spec section, level, name, status, and optional detail.

requirements.title: Conformance report
requirements.text: The conform package shall aggregate results into a report with binary, tool, version, language, spec version, and summary counts; HasFailures returns true only when a MUST check failed.

requirements.title: Conformance options
requirements.text: The conform package shall accept an injectable RunFunc to allow deterministic testing without a real binary on PATH.

requirements.title: Conformance runner
requirements.text: conform.Run shall locate the binary, scaffold a temp project, execute all conformance checks, and return a report.

requirements.title: Conformance rendering
requirements.text: The conform package shall render a report in text or json format, reporting RESULT:PASS or RESULT:FAIL.

requirements.title: Language detection
requirements.text: The conform package shall map binary names to language ids per §1.1 (gofusa→go, cfusa→c, cpfusa→cpp).

requirements.title: Common header validation
requirements.text: The conform package shall validate the §3.1 common header (schemaVersion, kind, tool, toolVersion, language, generatedAt) on every document.

requirements.title: Version check
requirements.text: The conform package shall check §9.1 version output matches the <tool> <semver> regex and optionally validates version --format json specVersion.

requirements.title: Init check
requirements.text: The conform package shall check §9.1 init creates .fusa.json and .fusa-reqs.json with valid JSON.

requirements.title: Check command validation
requirements.text: The conform package shall validate §4 check --format json: common header, nested location object, project-relative file paths, severity enum, ruleId regex, summary fields.

requirements.title: Trace command validation
requirements.text: The conform package shall validate §5 trace --format json: common header, requirements/tags/coverage keys, and all four coverage counters including secTestedRequirements.

requirements.title: Qualify command validation
requirements.text: The conform package shall validate §6 qualify --output: common header, total/passed/failed keys (not tests_passed/tests_failed), results[].result enum.

requirements.title: Release command validation
requirements.text: The conform package shall validate §7 release --output-dir writes sbom.json with common header, module, and components.

requirements.title: Audit-pack validation
requirements.text: The conform package shall validate §8 audit-pack produces a valid ZIP containing manifest.json with bare-hex sha256 fields.

requirements.title: Capabilities validation
requirements.text: The conform package shall validate §9.1 SHOULD capabilities --format json: common header, specVersion, commands.

requirements.title: Fingerprint algorithm
requirements.text: The conform package shall implement the §4.2 fingerprint algorithm: sha256(ruleId + U+001F + location.file + U+001F + normalizedMessage), with digit-run normalisation and whitespace collapsing.

requirements.title: Conform command
requirements.text: fusaops conform shall run x-FuSa spec conformance checks against a named binary, render the report in text or json, and exit non-zero when any MUST check fails.

requirements.title: GapReport type
requirements.text: The standards package shall define a GapReport type mirroring the §9.3 gap-report document with standard, objectives, and summary fields.

requirements.title: Objective status enum
requirements.text: The standards package shall define Objective with status values satisfied, partial, and gap; a consumer must map any unrecognised status to gap (fail-safe).

requirements.title: ComponentGap skipped recording
requirements.text: The standards package shall record a skipped reason for any component whose tool is unavailable or whose standards command fails, so coverage gaps remain visible.

requirements.title: Aggregate construction
requirements.text: The standards package shall aggregate ComponentGap entries into an Aggregate with standard id, project, generated timestamp, and all component results.

requirements.title: HasGaps predicate
requirements.text: Aggregate.HasGaps shall return true if and only if at least one reporting component has a non-zero gaps count in its Summary; nil or skipped components shall not count.

requirements.title: Text renderer
requirements.text: The standards package shall render an Aggregate as human-readable text showing per-component satisfied/partial/gaps counts and a RESULT: PASS|GAP|SKIP line.

requirements.title: JSON renderer
requirements.text: The standards package shall render an Aggregate as indented JSON, and RenderToFile shall write to a file or stdout.

requirements.title: CommandStandard alias
requirements.text: The standards package shall map CLI command names to canonical §2.4.1 standard ids; do178 maps to do178c.

requirements.title: DisplayName
requirements.text: The standards package shall expose a DisplayName function returning a human-readable label for each canonical standard id.

requirements.title: Summary recomputation
requirements.text: GapReport.RecomputeSummary shall derive Summary counts from Objectives when the existing Summary invariant does not hold, mapping any unrecognised status to gap (fail-safe per §9.3).

requirements.title: StandardsProvider capability
requirements.text: The adapter package shall define a StandardsProvider capability interface whose Standards method runs the tool's gap-report command for a given standard id and returns a decoded GapReport.

requirements.title: cmdAdapter Standards implementation
requirements.text: cmdAdapter shall implement StandardsProvider by shelling out to <tool> <standard> --format json and decoding the GapReport.

requirements.title: Standards roll-up
requirements.text: The orchestrator shall roll every applicable tool's §9.3 gap report for a given standard into one cross-language Aggregate, recording skipped components for unavailable or non-supporting tools.

requirements.title: ISO 26262 command
requirements.text: fusaops iso26262 shall roll up ISO 26262 gap reports across all applicable installed tools, render in text or json, and exit 1 under --strict when any objective has gap status.

requirements.title: IEC 61508 command
requirements.text: fusaops iec61508 shall roll up IEC 61508 gap reports across all applicable installed tools, render in text or json, and exit 1 under --strict when any objective has gap status.

requirements.title: DO-178C command
requirements.text: fusaops do178 shall roll up DO-178C gap reports across all applicable installed tools, mapping the do178 command name to the do178c canonical id, render in text or json, and exit 1 under --strict when any objective has gap status.

requirements.title: ComputeFingerprint canonical hash
requirements.description: The root package must export ComputeFingerprint(Finding) string that returns sha256:<64 hex> per x-FuSa spec §4.2, normalising digit runs in Message to # and collapsing whitespace.
requirements.rationale: Enables reproducible cross-run matching without requiring tools to emit fingerprints.

requirements.title: run.timeout configuration
requirements.description: Config.Run.Timeout must hold a duration string (e.g. 60s) applied as a per-adapter execution deadline.
requirements.rationale: Prevents hung tool invocations from blocking CI indefinitely.

requirements.title: run.workers configuration
requirements.description: Config.Run.Workers must hold a non-negative integer capping the number of adapters that run concurrently; zero means unlimited.
requirements.rationale: Allows resource-constrained environments to limit parallelism.

requirements.title: component pin configuration
requirements.description: Each ComponentConfig in scan.components must support an adapter field (tool name, overrides detection) and a timeout field (per-component duration override).
requirements.rationale: Enables monorepo sub-directory pinning to specific adapters with independent timeouts.

requirements.title: Parallel adapter execution
requirements.description: Run, RunTrace, RunSBOM, RunStandards, and RunAuditPack must execute per-adapter work in parallel goroutines, bounded by Options.Workers when > 0, each with Options.Timeout deadline when > 0.
requirements.rationale: Reduces total scan latency from sum-of-tools to max-of-tools.

requirements.title: Per-adapter context timeout
requirements.description: Each adapter goroutine must derive a child context with the applicable timeout (component-level overrides global) and cancel it on completion.
requirements.rationale: Isolates a hung adapter so others continue and the overall run still produces a report.

requirements.title: Component pinning orchestration
requirements.description: When Options.Components is non-empty, Run must scan each ComponentPin.Path independently and restrict to ComponentPin.Adapter when set, allowing the same tool to scan multiple sub-directories.
requirements.rationale: Supports monorepo layouts where multiple Go or C modules coexist under one root.

requirements.title: Baseline loading
requirements.description: LoadBaseline must parse both the FuSaOps aggregate report format (components[].findings) and the flat single-tool format (findings[]) and return a Baseline value.
requirements.rationale: Lets users store baselines from either a full fusaops check run or a per-tool check run.

requirements.title: Diff comparison
requirements.description: Compare must match findings by fingerprint (computing one via ComputeFingerprint when absent) and return Result{Added, Removed, Unchanged} deterministically sorted.
requirements.rationale: Enables reproducible CI gating independent of iteration order.

requirements.title: Diff rendering
requirements.description: Render must support text and json formats, emit a Gate: PASS/FAIL line, and reflect --strict mode (any new finding → FAIL, not just errors).
requirements.rationale: Provides human and machine-readable CI output with clear gate verdict.

requirements.title: fusaops diff command
requirements.description: fusaops diff --dir --baseline --format --output --strict --update-baseline must load a baseline, run the orchestrator, compare findings, render the result, exit 1 on gate failure, and optionally overwrite the baseline with the current run.
requirements.rationale: Exposes diff gating as a first-class CLI command suitable for CI steps.

requirements.title: Diff severity summary
requirements.description: Result.Summary must return per-severity counts for added and removed findings; text output must include the breakdown; JSON output must include a summary object and generatedAt timestamp.
requirements.rationale: Allows CI consumers to distinguish errors from warnings without parsing individual finding objects.

requirements.title: Baseline update
requirements.description: SaveBaseline must write current findings to a file in the flat baseline format; fusaops diff --update-baseline must call SaveBaseline after comparing.
requirements.rationale: Enables a rolling-baseline CI workflow where a passing diff updates its own baseline in place.

requirements.title: cpp-FuSa standards normalization
requirements.description: The cpp-FuSa adapter Standards must run <tool> <cmd> --output <tmp> (not --format json), map do178c→do178 subcommand name, and call RecomputeSummary on the decoded GapReport.
requirements.rationale: cpp-FuSa writes gap reports to a file rather than stdout and does not accept --format json; the adapter normalizes the invocation.

requirements.title: SecTestedRequirements coverage
requirements.description: trace.Coverage and AggregateCoverage must include a secTestedRequirements field (§5); ComponentTrace must expose SecTestedPct(); New() must sum and compute SecTestedPct across components.
requirements.rationale: Spec §5 requires four coverage counters including secTestedRequirements; FuSaOps must propagate the field from tool output through the aggregate so consumers can gate on security test coverage.

requirements.title: FilterGaps helper
requirements.description: FilterGaps must return a copy of an Aggregate with each component's Requirements slice reduced to only untraced or untested entries, preserving coverage totals. Used by fusaops trace --gaps.
requirements.rationale: Enables the --gaps flag to surface only actionable gaps without re-running the orchestrator.

requirements.title: fusaops trace coverage gates
requirements.description: fusaops trace must accept --gaps (show only untraced/untested requirements), --req-coverage N (fail when tracedPct < N), and --sec-tested N (fail when secTestedPct < N).
requirements.rationale: Spec §5 (line 594) defines these flags as part of the trace command surface; they provide threshold-based CI gates beyond the binary --strict flag.

requirements.title: ISO 21434 command
requirements.description: fusaops iso21434 shall roll up ISO 21434 gap reports across all applicable installed tools, render in text or json, and exit 1 under --strict when any objective has gap status.
requirements.rationale: Exposes ISO 21434 (automotive cybersecurity) compliance roll-up as a first-class CLI command.

requirements.title: UNECE command
requirements.description: fusaops unece shall roll up UNECE R155/R156 gap reports across all applicable installed tools, render in text or json, and exit 1 under --strict when any objective has gap status.
requirements.rationale: Exposes UNECE R155/R156 (vehicle cybersecurity management) compliance roll-up as a first-class CLI command.

requirements.title: IEC 62443 command
requirements.description: fusaops iec62443 shall roll up IEC 62443 gap reports across all applicable installed tools, render in text or json, and exit 1 under --strict when any objective has gap status.
requirements.rationale: Exposes IEC 62443 (industrial cybersecurity) compliance roll-up as a first-class CLI command; go-FuSa and cpp-FuSa both implement the iec62443 subcommand.

requirements.title: rust-FuSa adapter
requirements.description: FuSaOps shall provide a rust-FuSa adapter (rsfusa) that detects .rs files and delegates check/trace/qualify/release/audit-pack to rsfusa via the generic cmdAdapter path. The rsfusa binary produces spec v1.9 conformant JSON (ruleId + location object for check; flat tags array for trace) so no output normalisation is required.
requirements.rationale: Extends FuSaOps multi-language orchestration to Rust projects using rust-FuSa v0.2.0.

requirements.title: py-FuSa adapter
requirements.description: FuSaOps shall provide a py-FuSa adapter (pyfusa) that detects .py files and delegates check/trace/qualify/release/audit-pack to pyfusa via the generic cmdAdapter path. The pyfusa binary produces spec v1.9 conformant JSON so no output normalisation is required.
requirements.rationale: Extends FuSaOps multi-language orchestration to Python projects using py-FuSa v0.1.0 (alpha).

requirements.title: java-FuSa adapter
requirements.description: FuSaOps shall provide a java-FuSa adapter (jfusa) that detects .java files and delegates check/trace/qualify/release/audit-pack to jfusa via the generic cmdAdapter path. The jfusa binary produces spec v1.10 conformant JSON so no output normalisation is required.
requirements.rationale: Extends FuSaOps multi-language orchestration to Java projects using java-FuSa v0.1.0.

requirements.title: Policy model
requirements.description: FuSaOps shall define a Policy with a name and a list of Rules; each Rule optionally scopes to a language and/or tool and defines constraints: maxFindings, maxErrors, maxWarnings, requireStatus (PASS/WARN). LoadPolicy shall read and parse a JSON policy config file.
requirements.rationale: Enables orgs to codify safety gates (e.g. zero errors in Go, max 5 warnings across all languages) in a machine-checkable config file.

requirements.title: Policy report model
requirements.description: FuSaOps shall define a PolicyReport with per-rule RuleResult entries (rule, passed, message) and aggregate pass/fail counts; Status() shall return PASS or FAIL; HasFailures() shall return true when any rule failed.
requirements.rationale: Provides a structured, machine-readable policy evaluation outcome for CI gating.

requirements.title: Policy evaluation
requirements.description: policy.Evaluate shall run every rule against the AggregateReport, counting findings scoped to the rule's language/tool filters, and record PASS or FAIL with an explanatory message per rule.
requirements.rationale: The evaluation must be deterministic and produce actionable failure messages so engineers know exactly which rule failed and why.

requirements.title: Policy rendering
requirements.description: policy.Render shall write a PolicyReport in text (per-rule PASS/FAIL lines and RESULT line) or json format, rejecting unknown formats; RenderToFile shall write to a file or stdout.
requirements.rationale: Provides human-readable and machine-readable output for CI logs and audit records.

requirements.title: Policy command
requirements.description: fusaops policy --policy policy.json [--dir dir] [--format text|json] [--output file] shall load the policy, run the orchestrator, evaluate the policy against the report, render the result, and exit 1 when any rule fails.
requirements.rationale: Exposes org-wide policy enforcement as a first-class CLI command suitable for CI gates.

requirements.title: Fleet config model
requirements.description: FuSaOps shall define a Fleet Config with a project name and a list of Repo entries (name, dir, optional adapter); LoadConfig shall read and parse a JSON fleet config file.
requirements.rationale: Enables multi-repo orchestration from a single declarative config file.

requirements.title: Fleet report model
requirements.description: FuSaOps shall define a FleetReport with per-repo RepoResult entries (name, dir, status, counts, optional scan error) and aggregate totals; Status() shall return FAIL if any repo has FAIL/ERROR, WARN if any has WARN, PASS otherwise.
requirements.rationale: Aggregates per-repo scan outcomes into one fleet-level verdict for CI gating.

requirements.title: Fleet run
requirements.description: fleet.Run shall execute fusaops check against each repo in the config in parallel, aggregate results into a FleetReport, and record scan errors per repo without aborting the fleet run.
requirements.rationale: Parallel execution reduces fleet scan time to max-of-repos rather than sum-of-repos.

requirements.title: Fleet rendering
requirements.description: fleet.Render shall write a FleetReport in text (columnar table with per-repo status) or json format, rejecting unknown formats; RenderToFile shall write to a file or stdout.
requirements.rationale: Provides human-readable and machine-readable output for CI logs and programmatic consumers.

requirements.title: Fleet command
requirements.description: fusaops fleet --config fleet.json [--format text|json] [--output file] [--strict] shall load the fleet config, run check across all repos, render the fleet report, and exit 1 on FAIL (or on WARN under --strict).
requirements.rationale: Exposes multi-repo fleet scanning as a first-class CLI command suitable for org-level CI gates.

requirements.title: Status endpoint
requirements.description: The Server shall expose GET /api/v1/status returning a JSON object with status (PASS/WARN/FAIL/ERROR/PENDING), errors, warnings, and total counts for lightweight polling by CI gates and external monitors.
requirements.rationale: CI tools need a lightweight JSON endpoint to poll build status without parsing the full report.

requirements.title: Findings filter endpoint
requirements.description: The Server shall expose GET /api/v1/findings with optional query params severity, language, and tool that return a filtered JSON array of findings from the current cached report.
requirements.rationale: Enables CI tools and IDE plugins to query specific findings (e.g. only ERROR severity, only Go language) without parsing the full aggregate report.

requirements.title: Run snapshot model
requirements.description: FuSaOps shall define a Snapshot type recording a single check run outcome (runAt, status PASS/FAIL, total/error/warning/info counts, per-language summaries) and a FromReport function that builds a Snapshot from an AggregateReport.
requirements.rationale: A persistent record of each run outcome is required to render a severity trend over time.

requirements.title: Run history persistence
requirements.description: FuSaOps shall provide Store and Load functions for appending Snapshot records to .fusaops-history.jsonl (JSONL, one object per line) and reading back the most recent entries, trimming the file to at most MaxSnapshots=100 entries on each write. A missing file is not an error.
requirements.rationale: JSONL append is atomic and efficient; a fixed cap prevents unbounded disk growth.

requirements.title: Server history integration
requirements.description: The Server shall expose a WithHistoryDir(dir) method that, when set, causes each successful report compute to append a Snapshot to .fusaops-history.jsonl in dir.
requirements.rationale: Opt-in persistence via a fluent method avoids breaking the existing New() signature while enabling historical data collection in fusaops serve.

requirements.title: History HTTP routes
requirements.description: The Server shall expose /api/history (JSON array of Snapshots) and /history (HTML trend page showing last 30 runs with PASS/FAIL badges, per-severity counts, and a proportional severity bar) routes.
requirements.rationale: Provides both machine-readable and human-readable access to run history for CI integration and team dashboards.

requirements.title: HTTP Basic Auth middleware
requirements.description: The Server shall expose a WithAuth(user, pass string) fluent method that, when set, wraps all HTTP routes with Basic Auth enforcement via an authMiddleware. Requests with correct credentials pass through; missing or invalid credentials receive 401 Unauthorized.
requirements.rationale: Protects the dashboard and API from unauthenticated access in enterprise deployments without requiring an external proxy.

requirements.title: WWW-Authenticate challenge
requirements.description: The authMiddleware shall set the WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm=fusaops header on all 401 Unauthorized responses so browsers and HTTP clients can prompt for credentials.
requirements.rationale: Required by RFC 7617 to allow interactive authentication from browser clients.

requirements.title: Fleet dashboard integration
requirements.description: The Server shall expose a WithFleetConfig(path string) fluent method that, when set, runs a parallel fleet scan on each compute() call and caches the FleetReport. The Handler() shall register /fleet (HTML) and /api/fleet (JSON) routes when a fleet config is configured.
requirements.rationale: Enables a multi-repo fleet status view inside the fusaops serve dashboard without a separate fleet command.

requirements.title: Fleet HTML and JSON routes
requirements.description: The /fleet route shall render an HTML page showing the fleet project name, generation time, overall status badge, and a per-repo table (name, status badge, total/errors/warnings/infos). The /api/fleet route shall serve the cached FleetReport as JSON.
requirements.rationale: Provides both human-readable and machine-readable fleet status for team dashboards and CI polling.

requirements.title: HTTPS/TLS support
requirements.description: The Server shall expose a ListenAndServeTLS(addr, certFile, keyFile string) method that loads the X.509 certificate pair and serves the dashboard over TLS 1.2+ using tls.Listen. The fusaops serve CLI shall accept --tls-cert and --tls-key flags that enable HTTPS; --tls-key is required when --tls-cert is set.
requirements.rationale: HTTPS is required for enterprise deployments where the dashboard is exposed over a network.

requirements.title: fusaops serve --auth flag
requirements.description: The serve subcommand shall accept a --auth user:pass flag that enables HTTP Basic Auth on the dashboard. If the value does not contain a colon the command shall exit 1 with a descriptive error.
requirements.rationale: Gives operators a single-flag way to password-protect the serve dashboard.

requirements.title: fusaops serve --fleet flag
requirements.description: The serve subcommand shall accept a --fleet path flag that enables the fleet web dashboard at /fleet and /api/fleet.
requirements.rationale: Exposes the multi-repo fleet view inside the serve dashboard without requiring a separate command.

requirements.title: fusaops serve --tls-cert and --tls-key flags
requirements.description: The serve subcommand shall accept --tls-cert and --tls-key flags. When --tls-cert is set, --tls-key is required; the server switches to HTTPS via ListenAndServeTLS. Missing --tls-key exits 1 with a descriptive error.
requirements.rationale: Enables HTTPS without an external reverse proxy for enterprise deployments.

requirements.title: Read-only auth role
requirements.description: The Server shall support a read-only credential pair via WithAuthRO(user, pass string). When authentication is enabled, both rw (WithAuth) and ro (WithAuthRO) credentials are accepted. An ro user can access any route that does not mutate server state.
requirements.rationale: Enables operators to grant dashboard read access to stakeholders who should not be able to trigger re-scans.

requirements.title: Mutating route restriction
requirements.description: The authMiddleware shall reject ro credentials on mutating paths (/refresh) with 403 Forbidden. Read-write credentials retain full access to all routes.
requirements.rationale: Prevents read-only users from triggering expensive re-scans or state changes.

requirements.title: Request audit log
requirements.description: The Server shall expose a WithAuditLog(dir string) method. When set, the authMiddleware appends one auditEntry JSON record per authenticated request to .fusaops-audit.jsonl in dir. Each record includes timestamp, HTTP method, path, authenticated user, and response status code.
requirements.rationale: Audit trails are required for enterprise deployments to satisfy change-management and accountability requirements.

requirements.title: Audit entry schema
requirements.description: Each audit entry appended to .fusaops-audit.jsonl shall be a JSON object with fields: timestamp (RFC3339 UTC), method, path, user, status (HTTP status code). The file shall be created if it does not exist and appended to (never truncated) with mode 0600.
requirements.rationale: A stable schema and safe file mode allow external audit tools to parse and protect the log.

requirements.title: fusaops serve --auth-ro flag
requirements.description: The serve subcommand shall accept --auth-ro user:pass that sets read-only credentials on the server via WithAuthRO. A missing colon in the value shall exit 1 with a descriptive error.
requirements.rationale: Single-flag way to set a read-only viewer account without granting refresh access.

requirements.title: fusaops serve --audit-log flag
requirements.description: The serve subcommand shall accept --audit-log dir that enables request audit logging to .fusaops-audit.jsonl in the given directory.
requirements.rationale: Gives operators a single flag to enable access logging for compliance and debugging.

requirements.title: Multi-project config
requirements.description: FuSaOps shall define ProjectsConfig{Projects []ProjectConfig} and ProjectConfig{Name, Dir, Adapter string} as the JSON format for fusaops serve --projects. NewMulti(cfg, runner) creates a MultiServer with one projectEntry per project.
requirements.rationale: Teams managing multiple repositories benefit from a single serve command that watches all of them simultaneously.

requirements.title: Parallel multi-project scan
requirements.description: MultiServer.compute(ctx) shall run all project scans concurrently using one goroutine per project. ListenAndServe and Serve shall call compute before accepting requests.
requirements.rationale: Parallel execution prevents slow repos from delaying fast ones and matches the behaviour of fusaops fleet.

requirements.title: Multi-project overview routes
requirements.description: MultiServer.Handler() shall serve GET / as an HTML project overview grid (name, status badge, error/warning counts, link to detail page) and GET /api/projects as a JSON array of all project statuses. /healthz and /refresh are also registered.
requirements.rationale: Provides at-a-glance visibility across all projects from one URL.

requirements.title: Per-project detail pages
requirements.description: MultiServer.Handler() shall register GET /p/{name} for each configured project. The handler renders an HTML findings page (rule, severity, language, file, message) for that project. Unknown project names return 404.
requirements.rationale: Allows drilling into a specific project's findings from the overview without a separate serve process.

requirements.title: fusaops serve --projects flag
requirements.description: The serve subcommand shall accept --projects path that switches to multi-project mode using MultiServer. A missing or malformed file exits 1 with a descriptive error. All auth, ro, and audit-log flags apply equally to the MultiServer.
requirements.rationale: Single entry point for multi-project dashboard mode.

requirements.title: SVG status badge endpoint
requirements.description: The server shall expose GET /badge/status.svg returning a shields.io-style flat SVG badge with label 'fusaops' and message PASS/WARN/FAIL/pending/error colored green/yellow/red/gray respectively. Content-Type shall be image/svg+xml and Cache-Control shall be no-cache.
requirements.rationale: Embeddable status badge for README files and CI dashboards without polling the full report endpoint.

requirements.title: Per-project badge endpoint
requirements.description: MultiServer shall expose GET /badge/{name}/status.svg for each configured project, returning a badge labeled with the project name. The aggregate badge at /badge/status.svg uses the overall status across all projects.
requirements.rationale: Allows per-project embeddable badges in monorepo READMEs.

requirements.title: Webhook status-change notification
requirements.description: When configured via WithWebhook(url), the server shall POST a JSON payload {"status":"...","prev":"...","errors":N} to url whenever the aggregate status transitions between runs. The first compute does not fire (no prior state). The POST uses Content-Type application/json.
requirements.rationale: Enables push-based alerting without external polling, integrating with Slack, PagerDuty, and CI webhooks.

requirements.title: Webhook retry on failure
requirements.description: If the initial webhook POST fails, the server shall retry exactly once after a 2-second delay. Subsequent failures are silently dropped to avoid blocking the dashboard.
requirements.rationale: Provides basic reliability for transient network failures without unbounded retries.

requirements.title: fusaops serve --webhook flag
requirements.description: The serve subcommand shall accept --webhook url to configure status-change webhook notifications on the single-project Server. The flag is not available in --projects (multi-project) mode.
requirements.rationale: CLI entry point for webhook configuration.

requirements.title: Scheduled background rescan
requirements.description: Server and MultiServer shall support an optional refresh interval configured via WithRefreshInterval(d). When set, the server shall launch a background goroutine that calls compute() at every tick of d after the initial startup scan. A zero or negative interval disables scheduled rescans. The interval does not interrupt in-flight scans.
requirements.rationale: Enables the dashboard to stay current without manual /refresh requests in unattended deployments.

requirements.title: fusaops serve --refresh-interval flag
requirements.description: The serve subcommand shall accept --refresh-interval d (e.g. 5m, 1h) to configure Server.WithRefreshInterval. A non-positive or unparseable value shall exit 1 with a descriptive error. The flag applies to both single-project and multi-project (--projects) modes.
requirements.rationale: CLI entry point for scheduled rescan configuration.

requirements.title: OpenMetrics /metrics endpoint (single-project)
requirements.description: Server shall expose GET /metrics returning an OpenMetrics text exposition (Content-Type: text/plain; version=0.0.4; charset=utf-8) with at minimum: fusaops_findings_total{severity} for error/warning/info counts and fusaops_status with values 1=PASS, 2=WARN, 3=FAIL, 0=pending/error. Output shall end with # EOF.
requirements.rationale: Enables Prometheus/Grafana integration for safety metric dashboards without an additional exporter.

requirements.title: OpenMetrics /metrics endpoint (multi-project)
requirements.description: MultiServer shall expose GET /metrics returning per-project metrics with a project label on all time series (e.g. fusaops_findings_total{project="firmware",severity="error"}). Each project's metrics are aggregated independently.
requirements.rationale: Monorepo operators can track per-component safety metrics in a single Prometheus scrape target.

requirements.title: Suppression config format
requirements.description: A .fusaops-suppress.json file shall contain a JSON object with a 'suppressions' array. Each entry shall have 'fingerprint' (spec §4.2 fingerprint string), 'reason' (mandatory rationale string), and optional 'expires' (ISO-8601 date YYYY-MM-DD). Entries with empty fingerprints are ignored.
requirements.rationale: Teams require a documented, auditable way to acknowledge known findings without inflating the error count.

requirements.title: LoadConfig reads suppression config
requirements.description: suppression.LoadConfig(path) shall read and unmarshal the suppression config from path. An empty path shall return an empty config (zero-config path). A missing or malformed file shall return an error.
requirements.rationale: Zero-config path enables suppression to be optional with no CLI friction.

requirements.title: Filter partitions findings by active suppressions
requirements.description: suppression.Filter(findings, cfg, now) shall return (kept, suppressed) slices. A finding is suppressed when its Fingerprint matches an active suppression (not expired, date parseable). An expired suppression (or one with a malformed date) shall NOT suppress the finding. Findings without fingerprints are never suppressed.
requirements.rationale: Expiry ensures suppressions do not silently outlive their intended scope.

requirements.title: Orchestrator applies suppression before building the report
requirements.description: When Options.SuppressFile is set, Runner.Run() shall load the suppression config, apply Filter() to each component's findings, recompute component and global summaries from the kept findings, and set AggregateReport.Suppressed to the total count of suppressed findings. A missing or malformed suppress file shall return an error.
requirements.rationale: Suppression must be applied before report generation so all renderers and the check exit code reflect the true active finding count.

requirements.title: fusaops check/report --suppress-file flag
requirements.description: The check and report subcommands shall accept --suppress-file path to apply a suppression config. The path is forwarded to Options.SuppressFile. A missing or malformed file exits 1 with a descriptive error.
requirements.rationale: CLI entry point for finding suppression.
